name: Constitutive Modelling in Geotechnics
description: Fundamental relationships: coordinate system, sign conventions, concept of stresses and strains, stress transformation, equilibrium equations, moment equilibrium, principal stresses, invariants, octahedral stresses, volumetric and deviatoric stresses, stress-strain relationship; elasticity: isotropic, anisotropic, orthotropic, shear and bulk moduli, plane stress, plane strain and axisymmetric cases, Mohr circle, cylindrical coordinates, Airy’s stress function; nonlinear behaviour: importance of testing, stress paths, hyperbolic model; yielding: pi-plane, von Mises, Tresca and Mohr-Coulomb criteria; elastoplastic models: concept of plasticity, plastic hardening, plastic potentials, flow rule; cam-clay model: critical state line, stress dilatancy, prediction, applications; limit state analysis – lower and upper bound theorems, selected boundary value problems; introduction to viscoelastic models.
